Both estimates use the same heart rate. RULES is the simple threshold estimator; the difference shows what the model adds.

A reference night is a sleep session that another app (another watch, a ring, a sleep-lab app) wrote to Health Connect with real sleep stages: light, deep, REM. PulseStages estimates the same night from its heart rate and compares both. Sessions without stages, like the ones OHealth writes, cannot serve as references.
Mean error per night: deep %1$s, REM %2$s, awake %3$s.
Accuracy: share of the reference\'s time in a stage that the estimate got right (recall). Precision: share of the estimate\'s time in a stage that the reference confirms.
Rows: reference stage. Columns: estimate. Each cell: number of 30-second chunks and share of the row.
Calibration fits a personal model on these reference nights (the latest ones are held out to measure it) and uses it for every later estimate. Nights estimated before become stale.
Personalization is switched off (Settings → Personalization). Turn it on to calibrate.
Switching back to the global model…
%1$s. No night was left over to measure the effect.
Calibration was not possible: the reference nights have no labelled epochs with heart rate.
The personal model is switched off and estimates use the global models again. Nights estimated with the personal model become stale.
Not estimated: too little heart rate
